races.name: Betfred 'turbo Boost' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Em Four
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist trained by Jamie Osborne with Saffie aboard; ran just seven days ago and form figures of 357851 suggest inconsistency, but that sole win came over 6f on Good — the softer surface today is unlikely to enhance her chances of generating a finishing kick.|
runners_data.comment: Em Four landed a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform from stall five carrying 140 lb, with our rating of 78 marking him a leading threat; the risk is that five of his last six starts show he can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Logi Bear
runners_data.note: John Butler's three-year-old carries a hood and genuine hold-up profile; came back from a 16-day break with a win over 6f on Standard and has placed on Good twice — the soft ground today is well within range and David Probert's booking is a positive signal.|
runners_data.comment: Logi Bear arrives on the back of a win last time out and a runner-up finish two starts back, making him the form pick of the field. He has run over today's trip and going before, and 16 days between runs suggests he is fresh and ready to go again.

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's five-year-old is a true hold-up horse whose last win came over 6f on Soft — directly relevant form — but the crowded rear means he has been pushed onto the map in a midfield slot he won't naturally occupy; his style-fit in this shape is compromised and he'll need to race closer than ideal to land a blow.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Twirler has been in patchy form of late — unplaced last time out and winning only once in her last six starts — though she has experience of today's distance and going, and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround carrying 131 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old has no soft-ground history on record and all recent form has come on Good or Good to Firm; squeezed to a midfield position on the map because this is a genuinely hold-up dominated field, his true position will likely be further back than shown and ground conditions add uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Cayman Tai has run over today's trip and going before, and a third four starts back hints at some ability, but he has been winless in recent starts and his trainer has yet to land a winner in the last 14 days, making confidence hard to muster.

runners_data.name: Proof
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' three-year-old carries a tongue-tie, is 69 days fresh and has been beaten 13 lengths in recent starts, though that sole win came over 5f on Standard; shunted to midfield on the map despite being a hold-up type — Jason Watson may push him forward to track the leader, which is where he'd need to be to pose a threat.|
runners_data.comment: Proof has been out of the frame in four of his last five starts, and 69 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he does have experience over today's trip and a win in recent form shows ability is somewhere in there.

runners_data.name: Perfect Location
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's three-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner here and won over 6f on Soft earlier in the season — the most directly applicable piece of form in the race; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes over from the saddle 49 days after last run, and while the style-fit flag notes he may race somewhat out of role by being alone on the lead, uncontested front-running on this flat track is a significant tactical asset.|
runners_data.comment: Perfect Location won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going conditions, giving her a solid platform from stall two carrying 131 lb; the main worry is that fifth last time out suggests she may need to recapture that winning form quickly.

runners_data.name: Harry's Halo
runners_data.note: Kevin and Lauren Frost's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with his best recent form figures arriving on Soft (two thirds in last five) and who has been off 84 days; the longer break is a note of caution but soft ground suits him and a 5lb claim from Seamus Cronin eases the weight burden — he needs the race to develop into a proper test to get involved.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts — third on each of his last two starts — make Harry's Halo a leading threat despite being yet to win in recent starts, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the main concern is a layoff of 84 days.

races.paceDynamic: Perfect Location is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, energy-conserving gallop on Good to Soft ground at Epsom. That uncontested lead on a flat six-furlong track is a meaningful tactical advantage — a horse that can dictate its own fractions from the front without being harassed rarely burns unnecessary energy, and the soft-ish ground will reward those who travel economically rather than those who have to chase. The hold-up contingent — Em Four, Logi Bear, Twirler, Cayman Tai, Proof and Harry's Halo — are all trying to come from off the pace, meaning the race shape strongly favours Perfect Location and any horse prominent enough to track without getting into a battle. This race shape holds far more genuine hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear, and of those redistributed to a midfield position on the map, Proof and Twirler are the most likely to actually push forward and secure a tracking role, with Cayman Tai and Harry's Halo the truest closers in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Location goes unchallenged to the front and controls fractions throughout on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: Perfect Location sets a comfortable pace, conserves energy through the first three furlongs and simply has more left to give in the final two than any hold-up rival can generate; the uncontested lead on flat Epsom six is a significant edge when no rival forces a true test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides slower than expected, stretching the race out and giving hold-up horses enough time to generate momentum.
scenarios.body: A genuinely soft surface would blunt Perfect Location's advantage and reward those who travel smoothly in behind before producing a sustained late run; the horses with soft-ground form credentials and tactical speed off the bridle become relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up type secures an unplanned prominent position early and benefits from the controlled pace.
scenarios.body: Proof or Twirler, pushed forward from their natural hold-up role into a tracking position just off Perfect Location, find themselves in the ideal spot to challenge turning for home without having burned energy scrubbing; this shape suits horses able to quicken from second or third.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Contested Pace
scenarios.trigger: If two or more runners unexpectedly contest the lead, creating a genuinely strong early gallop that blows the race wide open.
scenarios.body: An unplanned pace battle would neutralise Perfect Location's front-running advantage and make the race more of a test of raw stamina in the ground, potentially gifting a well-handicapped closer a clean passage to win; this is the least likely shape given the clear split between one front-runner and a hold-up dominated field.

watchPoints.text: Perfect Location — if Pierre-Louis Jamin gets a clean break and settles alone in front, monitor whether any rival attempts to press early; if none do by the two-furlong marker, Perfect Location is in full control of its own destiny.

Proof — 69 days off the track and inconsistent form make him a volatility factor; if Jason Watson pushes him prominently to track the leader rather than accepting the hold-up role the map flags, he could either capitalise on the shape or get caught flat-footed late.

Harry's Halo — an 84-day absence combined with the longest layoff in the field means fitness is a genuine concern despite soft-ground form; watch how he travels in the early stages as a guide to whether the break has left its mark.

Twirler and Cayman Tai — both are true hold-up types pushed onto the map in a midfield position; if the field fans wide early and these two cannot find cover or rhythm, they may end up racing in an awkward no-man's land between the leader and the true closers, neither tracking effectively nor finishing strongly.

races.name: Irish Ebf Restricted Maiden Stakes (for Horses In Bands C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Red Tail
runners_data.note: Shaped with promise when second over 6f at Goodwood on Good ground last time and the step up to 7f looks a logical progression; Richard Hannon yard is winless from 37 runners over 14 days but the form angle here is positive if the Good to Soft surface doesn't blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Artemis Star
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, she is the pace-setter everything else revolves around; ran 3rd over 8f and 5th over 6f on Good so the 7f trip seems a workable middle-ground, and with Robert Havlin aboard and the Muir & Grassick yard in 2-from-15 form over 14 days, she carries genuine each-way claims if she controls proceedings.

runners_data.name: Lightenings Legacy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with headgear flagged 'v' (visor), which often sharpens a free-going type and may help her travel more economically from the rear; ran 6th and 9th in her two starts but those came on Good and Standside tracks, so the softer ground here is a potential plus if she stays the trip.

runners_data.name: Taranis
runners_data.note: Unraced and therefore the biggest unknown in the field — going is flagged UNKNOWN so any assumption about her soft-ground aptitude is guesswork; Eve Johnson Houghton is 3 from 27 in 14 days and Charles Bishop is a capable pilot, but this is pure projection until seen on a racecourse.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Desire
runners_data.note: Fourth on debut over 7f on Good ground suggests she handles the trip and showed promise, and the Amanda Perrett/David Probert combination is worth noting; however, her true running style is hold-up and she is being mapped to midfield because the field has more backmarkers than the race shape can house at the rear, meaning she will race in a less natural position and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Golden Caturra
runners_data.note: Back-to-back fourths on Good ground over 6f gives a consistent if unspectacular profile, and the step up to 7f on softer ground could unlock improvement; John Gallagher is 1 from 8 in 14 days and Kaiya Fraser is an apprentice, so winning from a hold-up position in a steadily-run race will require a disciplined ride and a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Summer Triangle
runners_data.note: Twice second over 6-7f on Good ground gives her a solid form profile relative to her OR of 71, which is markedly lower than the rest of the field; her genuine hold-up style is compromised by redistribution to midfield — she holds natural form credentials but the style mismatch and the class gap make this a tough ask, and the style-fit discount is relevant.

races.paceDynamic: Artemis Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no confirmed rival to press her, she should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop on Good to Soft ground over Epsom's flat seven furlongs. With Artemis Star setting a sustainable tempo unchallenged, the race is unlikely to develop the fierce early pace that would bring true hold-up horses into their own; instead, a premium is placed on horses who can track the leader at close quarters and produce a sustained finish rather than a late swooping run. The field does contain more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Angel Of Desire and Summer Triangle are genuine back-of-the-field types who will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural, meaning neither is operating in their optimal role. This race shape clearly favours hold-up-to-midfield types who can sit just off Artemis Star's controlled tempo and pick her off in the final two furlongs, rather than those needing a truly strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Artemis Star Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Artemis Star leads uncontested from the off and sets a steady, controlled tempo that suits a prominent racer tracking in behind.
scenarios.body: Artemis Star dictates on her own terms, and a horse sitting second or third can benefit from a race run without pressure before delivering a sustained challenge from two furlongs out; the Good to Soft surface rewards those with stamina and a smooth passage rather than raw finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sustainable enough that a midfield horse travelling well throughout can produce a strong final furlong to collar the front-runner close home.
scenarios.body: A steady gallop followed by a gradual wind-up from two out gives a horse settled in the middle third of the field time to pick up momentum on the soft surface; the winner here would be one that handles the ground well and has the stamina to sustain its run to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Artemis Star goes off faster than anticipated, burning herself out in the back straight and leaving the door ajar for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Even with the redistribution caveat, if genuine attrition sets in through the first half of the race a horse coming from the rear could thread through tired rivals; however, Angel Of Desire and Summer Triangle are racing out of their natural position so this scenario is structurally undermined by their suboptimal placement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Break, Unknown Factor
scenarios.trigger: If a maiden-field scrimmage at the start or erratic early running scrambles the anticipated shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced horses like Taranis, B Double U, and Red Tail carry significant unknown quantities given their limited form profiles, and a messy race could see an unexposed type bolt in from an unlikely position; this scenario carries the lowest probability precisely because the pace map is relatively straightforward with a lone front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch Artemis Star's opening furlong — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged she becomes a serious each-way proposition as the race revolves entirely around her pace judgement.

Summer Triangle and Angel Of Desire are true hold-up horses being forced closer to the pace than is ideal; if either is crowded or forced wide in the early stages their chance is materially damaged before the race develops.

Taranis is unraced and completely unknown — any wide draw, slow break, or greenness under pressure could see her produce an unpredictable run that scrambles the field's anticipated positions in the first two furlongs.

Golden Caturra and Lightenings Legacy both wear headgear and are stepping up in trip; monitor their early demeanour in the paddock — if either settles well it would boost confidence that the softer ground and longer trip will bring improvement.

races.name: Betfred 'the Classic Bookmaker' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist for Muir & Grassick who has been well beaten in recent starts, with the single win in his last five coming on Good ground at 7f — soft conditions here are not a concern but his current form is poor, and with no strong pace to aim at his late challenge faces a significant structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Morte Point won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, giving him a solid platform from stall three off a fair weight; the worry is that he has been out of the frame in all three subsequent runs.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride for a Watson yard 2-from-20 over 14 days, and this 4yo has placed on soft ground before at 7f; a natural prominent racer, she is well-placed to take full advantage of sitting close to a lone, uncontested front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a runner-up five starts back, Aurora Majesty returns on a quick turnaround carrying 138 lb from stall two, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; winless in his last five, he must convert that placed form, but our rating of 92 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Kisskodi
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's 4yo has winning form on soft and on Tapeta at 7f, suggesting versatility, and George Wood's claim could be useful at the weights; Kisskodi's prominent style slots neatly into the likely race shape, and two wins and two places from five soft/similar-going starts is the standout soft-ground record in this field.
runners_data.comment: Kisskodi won two starts back but has looked less convincing either side of that success, finishing fifth and then eighth in his last two, so recapturing that form is the key ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 136 lb from stall five is his hand.

runners_data.name: New Vega
runners_data.note: The Crisfords' 3yo is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will control the tempo, but she is racing slightly out of role as a confirmed front-runner with a STYLE_FIT flag, and her soft-ground profile from a single run (4th) does little to inspire confidence she can sustain her lead throughout the 7f.
runners_data.comment: Rated 7 of 8 on our figures, New Vega faces a stiff task, and a fifth last time out does little to inspire confidence after 44 days off; she does hold experience over today's trip and was a winner three starts back, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 8yo held a true hold-up role in recent starts and fades in finishes — he ran just two days ago, which is an obvious freshness concern, and with a REDISTRIBUTED tag reflecting that he will struggle to get his preferred position in this field, his chance is materially weakened.
runners_data.comment: Rhoscolyn has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 91 puts him right in contention from stall one, yet he arrives just two days after his last outing and is winless in recent starts — a concerning combination.

runners_data.name: Naval Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke sends out this 3yo with genuine soft-ground winning form (won on soft over 6f) and two wins from his last five, and Sam James is a capable handler; his hold-up style is compromised by the lack of a searching gallop, but if any closer has the class to make up ground it is Naval Light.
runners_data.comment: Naval Light won two of his last five starts, with back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and he brings experience of today's trip and going into the equation; the concern is that seventh last time out leaves his current form under a question mark.

runners_data.name: Do Bronxs
runners_data.note: Loughnane's 3yo has a legitimate hold-up profile but is a true closer redistributed into a midfield map position because the field is stacked at the rear — his best efforts have come in races with genuine pace, and a slow, controlled tempo set by a lone front-runner is precisely the shape that works against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Do Bronxs does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his second last time out offers some encouragement; however, that eighth two starts back is harder to ignore, and 131 lb from stall seven adds further pressure on a mark of 86.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo is genuinely a prominent-racing type whose natural position has been pushed back in the mapping due to congestion — her best form at 7f on Good ground shows she can race handily, but with a STYLE_FIT flag and the likely battle for early positions ahead of her, she arrives as a 77-rated runner already squeezed out of her preferred race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Velvet Rhythm faces a stiff ask, and one unplaced effort in her last six starts gives pause, though she does return quickly fit from just seven days ago and has run over today's trip before.

races.paceDynamic: New Vega is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in an eight-runner field over Epsom's 7f on Good To Soft ground, she is likely to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable tempo without being seriously pressed for the lead. Aurora Majesty and Kisskodi will attempt to track closely in behind, while the hold-up brigade of Naval Light, Morte Point and the true closers will be forced to settle further back than ideal given the lack of a truly searching gallop. With soft ground slowing things down and a lone pace-setter dictating from the front, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce entering the straight, rather than genuine hold-up horses needing a strong, relentless pace to reel the field in. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can physically accommodate — Velvet Rhythm, Do Bronxs and Rhoscolyn are genuine pace or prominent sorts who are likely to find themselves further back than suits, reducing their chance of producing a telling late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If New Vega sets a steady, uncontested pace and the closers struggle to generate momentum on soft ground.
scenarios.body: New Vega dictates throughout at an economical gallop, and Aurora Majesty or Kisskodi — tracking immediately behind — are ideally placed to swoop past in the final furlong before the genuine hold-up horses can close. Soft ground blunts late runs and rewards the horses racing in the first three, making the prominent profile the dominant winning shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Sustains Lead
scenarios.trigger: If New Vega's solo lead proves completely unassailable and no chasing horse finds enough acceleration to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Racing out of a natural lead role at a controlled tempo on soft ground, New Vega could simply conserve energy and sprint clear in the final two furlongs before the pack can organise a challenge. The Good To Soft conditions suit a horse who settles well and does not need to be asked for a sharp acceleration, rewarding those who can maintain their cruising speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Front
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and the hold-up horses get a proper test to aim at.
scenarios.body: Naval Light, who has winning form on soft ground and has shown she can rattle home late when conditions suit, would be the primary beneficiary if the gallop quickens and the leaders tire approaching the final furlong. Morte Point's hold-up style earns its keep only in this shape, though his recent form figures make his chance speculative even if the race sets up perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace Causes Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks into an uneven, stop-start gallop with multiple horses jostling for positions in the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: A confused early pace could scramble the race order entirely, negating the advantages of both prominent and hold-up racers, and hand the race to whichever horse settles best and delivers the cleanest run through the pack. Kisskodi, who has won on soft ground and holds a tactically versatile profile, could benefit from the disorder more than most in this low-probability scenario.

watchPoints.text: New Vega's unchallenged lead could produce a pace that is too slow to stretch the field, handing the race to the first horse to quicken off her quarters in the straight — watch how hard Aurora Majesty and Kisskodi press her from the two-furlong pole.

Rhoscolyn ran just two days ago and faces a gruelling turnaround; watch in the parade ring for any signs of staleness that could confirm a no-hoper in an already difficult tactical scenario for hold-up types.

Velvet Rhythm is a genuine prominent racer who may find herself blocked out of her natural position by Aurora Majesty and Kisskodi — watch the first two furlongs to see whether Saffie Osborne can push forward or is forced to settle off the pace.

Naval Light's soft-ground form is the best in the field among the hold-up horses, and if the early tempo is stronger than anticipated, watch whether Sam James positions him closer than his usual hold-up role to compensate for the likely lack of a true test.

Do Bronxs has twice finished second in stronger-paced races — watch whether Hector Crouch attempts to push forward from his natural hold-up position if he can see the pace is too slow to make ground from deep.

races.name: Betfred 'nifty 50' Amateurs' Derby Handicap Stakes (for Gentleman Amateur Jockeys) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Sweet Reward
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with course form at the trip, Jonathan Portman's 2/19 yard returns temper confidence but James Hills jr is competent; the horse has no soft-ground wins in recent history (0W0P in similar going) and has been running over shorter recently, making the step back to 1m4f a query.
runners_data.comment: Sweet Reward won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories three and four runs ago, and has experience of today's going, but he arrives after consecutive disappointing efforts and a demanding 165 lb burden makes improvement a tall order.

runners_data.name: Gordon Grey
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by George Baker, PW Mullins aboard adds serious amateur class; has won over 12f on Good and has soft-ground experience though his recent form shows a long absence of 86 days and only one placing in soft going across 15 runs — stamina sound, freshness a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Great Bedwyn
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Richard Hannon, most recent runs show a pattern of placed efforts at 12f on Good ground; the trip and surface look fine and 16 days since last run suggests freshness, though the yard has gone 0/37 in the past fortnight which is a significant trainer flag.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and third two starts back, Great Bedwyn arrives as our top-rated runner on 91 and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims as the one to beat; a trainer in a difficult spell of form is the one reservation.

runners_data.name: Son Of Man
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type who has won and placed over 12f on Standtrack surfaces; Good to Soft going is a genuine unknown (0W2P in similar) but has the right style for a strong-pace race, and Jim Boyle's record at this distance is solid — 19 days since last run keeps him fresh.
runners_data.comment: Son Of Man arrives on the back of a third and a second in the two starts before last, showing consistent form at this level, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the risk is his last two runs have yielded a blank and a ninth.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran just nine days ago, which is a freshness concern over a stiff 1m4f in testing conditions; has headgear (tongue tie) and Jamie Osborne's yard has been 2/11 in the last fortnight — the Epsom straight will demand energy he may not have fully recovered.
runners_data.comment: Epictetus landed a win two starts back but was a well-beaten sixth last time out, and 160 lb is a stern ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, yet that recent regression makes him a case of wait and see.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: Front-runner from William Haggas, a formidable yard that has been operating at 8/46 recently; has placed in soft ground (1P from 3 runs) and stays the trip, but as one of three confirmed leaders must share the early workload — controlling the pace without burning out is the key challenge.
runners_data.comment: Divine Knight has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third in two of his last five starts, and returns here on familiar distance and going terms after a 30-day break; winless in recent starts is the concern, but his rating of 88 marks him out as a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Devil In The Sky
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed in soft ground five times from 15 attempts and handles 12-16f comfortably; Gary & Josh Moore have been in 3/28 form and the horse's consistent placing profile (43-444 recent form) suggests reliability without a big winning threat unless conditions uniquely suit.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Devil In The Sky has been consistently placed in recent starts, finishing third four starts back among a sequence of fourths, and arrives here 48 days fresh carrying 157 lb with more to offer.

runners_data.name: Yaa Min
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 4-year-old lightly campaigned on turf good ground, with one soft-going start yielding 1W from 12 appearances; Hayley Burton's yard has had zero runners in the past fortnight so no recent data, but the horse has been running frequently and trips over 12f have suited.
runners_data.comment: Placed third in two of his last three starts but unable to convert, Yaa Min has experience of today's trip and conditions and returns on a quick turnaround of 15 days; the 157 lb burden is the chief concern for a gelding rated 79 officially.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel I
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear (cheekpieces), won over 12f on Good ground recently and placed once in soft — but Gihan Arnolda's yard has been 0/5 in 14 days and the horse's record over extended trips (20f) is mixed; the 1m4f is probably the ideal trip within this string.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back give Damascus Steel I some credibility, but an eighth last time out and a significant gap between his official mark and our rating make him hard to fancy at the foot of these rankings, though he has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Dancing Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has won twice and placed four times on soft going across 14 runs — the best soft-ground profile in the race; Roger Teal's yard is 4/12 in recent form, headgear (cheekpieces) applied, and the 4-year-old is lightly weighted at OR 75, making this a genuinely interesting profile for the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Tiger has run over today's trip and going, and his two seconds in his last three starts show he can find the principals, though a fourth last time out after 39 days off is a slight concern; 153 lb is no easy burden for a horse rated 75.

runners_data.name: Curran
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won multiple times over 12-14f including on Good ground; Rod Millman's yard is 4/23 and the horse is fit on 25 days, but as the lowest-weighted of the three leaders he must fight for position early in a three-way pace battle that could cost him late.
runners_data.comment: Boasts a win two starts back and a runner-up finish last time out, and has experience over today's trip and conditions, but 151 lb is a stern burden and he sits mid-division on ratings, suggesting a place rather than victory is the likeliest outcome.

runners_data.name: Crooked Path
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-hold-up type who has won over soft and heavy ground and stays 16f; James Owen's yard is 2/41 in the fortnight which dampens confidence, and the step back to 1m4f from longer trips is a query — but recent winning form and versatility of ground give him residual interest.
runners_data.comment: Crooked Path won last time out but that single success in his last five starts, combined with a trainer firing at just 5%, makes him hard to fancy here, and a 150 lb burden does him no favours, though he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Edward Sexton
runners_data.note: Won his last start over 14f on Good ground for Gary & Josh Moore, naturally a hold-up type but pushed into midfield on the map because true hold-up berths are congested in this field; his soft-going record is thin (0W2P from 10 runs) and the amateur jockey David Dunsdon adds uncertainty, so the repositioning tempers his realistic chance.
runners_data.comment: Edward Sexton won last time out which catches the eye, but that single success sits amid a run of poor efforts in recent starts, he ranks near the foot of our assessments here, and the 148 lb burden makes it hard to fancy him reversing those fortunes.

runners_data.name: Seeking Charles
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up performer who has placed twice on Good ground at 12f, drawn into midfield representation here because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with closers; Mark Usher's 1/11 recent record is modest, and the horse's record in soft going and at extended trips (16f+) has been poor, making the true-pace scenario a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Seeking Charles has shown some consistency — third two starts back and runner-up last time out — but ranked 11 of 14 on our figures and carrying 145 lb, he faces a stiff task, though distance and going experience count in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, and Curran are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop over Epsom's 1m4f on Good to Soft ground — a combination that will test stamina ruthlessly from an early stage. The three leaders are unlikely to yield to one another, meaning they will push each other along through Tattenham Corner and down the straight, with the pace unlikely to collapse at any point. This sustained tempo sets up the race ideally for hold-up and late-finishing types who can conserve energy in the first half and pick up the pieces when the leaders begin to tie up inside the final two furlongs. Edward Sexton and Seeking Charles are genuine hold-up horses by nature but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field's rear is crowded; Great Bedwyn, Son Of Man, Epictetus, and Dancing Tiger — authentic hold-up runners who should secure closer to their natural position — are the profiles this race shape favours most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out by halfway, leaving genuine hold-up horses to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, and Curran set a fierce early gallop that drains their reserves approaching the straight, handing advantage to those settled off the pace; horses like Great Bedwyn and Dancing Tiger, both adept at finishing strongly on soft ground, are ideally positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Thin The Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed front-runners dictates without being seriously pushed and completes wire to wire.
scenarios.body: Gordon Grey has led and won over 12f on Good ground before and Patrick Mullins is a supremely polished amateur jockey who could manage the pace cannily; if Divine Knight or Curran fade leaving Gordon Grey with daylight, his stamina credentials at the trip could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the true front-runners set a strong but not suicidal pace and prominent-positioned types land the decisive blow.
scenarios.body: Sweet Reward and Devil In The Sky are both confirmed prominent racers who could sit just off the leaders and strike when the front three begin to fade; on soft ground at this trip, a prominent position with a clean run into the straight often proves optimal at Epsom.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Ups Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly ferocious and the closers need every yard of the straight to finish.
scenarios.body: Son Of Man and Epictetus are genuine hold-up performers who would benefit most from a true slog, though both have modest form in soft conditions and their amateur jockeys add an element of timing uncertainty; Seeking Charles, while a natural hold-up type racing partially out of role, could also factor if everything falls right.

watchPoints.text: Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, and Curran will all want the lead from the outset — watch for a fierce battle for position in the first furlong that could produce a suicidal early gallop, dramatically increasing the chance of a late-finishing winner.

Great Bedwyn's trainer Richard Hannon has sent out zero winners from 37 runners in the past 14 days — if that slump reflects a yard not firing, Great Bedwyn's placed form could flatter what he actually delivers today.

Epictetus ran just nine days ago; in soft ground over 1m4f with an amateur jockey, recovery time matters — monitor market confidence to see if connections are genuinely expecting a big run or simply filling the field.

Dancing Tiger has the standout soft-ground form record in this race (2W4P across 14 runs on the surface) and is lightly weighted — if the pace genuinely demolishes the front-runners, his trajectory from the rear of midfield is the one to track into the straight.

Patrick Mullins aboard Gordon Grey is a significant jockey booking by amateur standards — if Mullins can nurse the pace rather than fight the other two front-runners, Gordon Grey becomes considerably more dangerous than his recent form suggests.

races.name: Stanley Wootton Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Drops back from 12f to a likely-suitable 10f trip after a mixed recent spell including a win; Jason Watson takes the ride for the in-form Cunha yard (6 wins from 26 in 14 days), and his prominent style suits tracking Trio, though his soft-going record from a single run (1/9, no wins) offers limited confidence on today's surface.
runners_data.comment: Hengest boasts three wins in his last six starts, including back-to-back victories, and has run over today's trip before, while 37 days off should leave him fresh; the risk is that his last two outings have been unplaced efforts that suggest he may need things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's patient placement is always worth noting — a winner two runs ago over 10f on Good, he drops back from 12f and switches to hold-up tactics with Dylan Hogan; his soft-going form is absent from recent runs but class and Prescott's precision make him a credible closer if the pace obliges.
runners_data.comment: Almekarem ran a cracker last time out, finishing second, and he landed a win three starts back to underline his ability; he has run over today's trip and a 19-day turnaround looks sharp enough, though that seventh two starts back is the form to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Perfect Scoundrel
runners_data.note: Three consecutive places including a win and a second over this sort of trip, and some soft-ground experience (3/9f/SOF), makes him one of the more solid pace-fit horses in the race; Robert Havlin's booking is positive, and his prominent style means he will naturally slot in behind Trio and have every chance if the steady gallop sets up a sustained finish.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and placed in two of his three most recent starts, Perfect Scoundrel arrives in good nick though 46 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 139 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Arthur's Realm
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has been running in soft company frequently (12 runs on soft, 1W2P) and whose best recent runs have come in those conditions, though he has finished no better than fifth in his last five; the headgear flag (p) is noted, and Gihan Arnolda's yard has sent no runners into the 14-day form window, making this a less confident angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Arthur's Realm nonetheless carries a compelling profile into this — our ratings rank him clear of the field, and he has run over today's trip and going before, giving connections solid grounding; 87 days off is the one query.

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has a solid base form including a win from 10 runs on Good, but his true racing style is hold-up and he has been moved forward on the map because of the field's congestion at the rear; Saffie Osborne takes the ride, and his soft-going exposure is minimal (1 run), with the STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 flagging a meaningful cost if he cannot operate from his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Mao Shang Wong shaped well when second three starts back and arrives here on a sound 28-day break with experience of today's distance and going in his favour; the worry is that he has struggled to recapture that form since, finishing seventh and fifth in his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Double Red
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's five-year-old has a prominent tag and consistent placed form over 10-12f on Good, though all five recent history runs are on Good ground and today's softish conditions represent a query; headgear (p) is flagged, David Probert retains the ride, and his yard has been quiet in the 14-day window.
runners_data.comment: Double Red has run over today's trip and going before and returns off a 25-day break, but his fifth last time out and only one win in his last six starts suggest he faces a stiff ask from 136 lb despite a draw from stall three.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, and Eve Johnson Houghton has placed him on a sharp upward trajectory (two consecutive wins); his form is over shorter trips (7-8f) and today's step up to 10f on soft ground is an open question, but his ability to control the pace from the front makes him structurally important to the entire race shape regardless of whether he stays the trip.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures and carrying 134 lb from stall ten, Trio faces a stiff ask, though she does bring winning form into this, scoring twice in her last six starts, and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Crystal Pier
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old showed a win at 8f on Soft (STA) and has placed over 10f on Good, and the trainer is in good current form (6/38 in 14 days); headgear (t) is noted, and Hector Crouch's booking is competent — he is a hold-up type who will need the pace to collapse or quicken sharply to get involved from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's five-year-old has consistent placed form over 10f on Good but all recent runs are on Good ground, offering zero soft-going evidence; his natural style is hold-up but he has been placed in midfield on the map because of the crowded rear — the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.93 reflects that racing in a position that is not his natural one is a genuine cost, and Pat Cosgrave will need to manage the compromise carefully.
runners_data.comment: Hello Cotai arrives ranked bottom but one on our figures and has managed just one win in his last six starts, with back-to-back fourths in his most recent outings giving little encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: A three-year-old with three wins in his last five but all on Good or Standard, with no soft-going runs recorded; Simon Dow's yard is lightly active (1/10 in 14 days) and Joe Leavy's claim may help with the weight, but as a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91, his chance is materially dependent on circumstances that are unlikely to arise naturally in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a speed rating that gives little encouragement, Sail On Sailor is hard to fancy despite a productive recent run of form that includes three wins in his last six starts, most recently a fifth last time out after 39 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Trio is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the gate, Charles Bishop can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Epsom's 1m2f trip on Good To Soft ground. Hengest and Perfect Scoundrel are the most likely to track him from prominent positions, but neither has the natural pace or mandate to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning Trio's sectionals will be self-selected and measured. The soft-ish underfoot conditions reinforce a steadier early tempo that rewards those who travel well through the race rather than those who need a frenetic gallop to close the gap late. This race shape squarely favours prominent racers who can sit just behind Trio, stay balanced through Epsom's undulations, and produce a sustained finish — hold-up runners face an uphill task unless the pace quickens significantly mid-race. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Mao Shang Wong, Sail On Sailor, and Hello Cotai are redistributed to midfield but are true closers who are unlikely to secure anything like their natural position given how few horses are ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trio Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Trio gets a clean break and sets an uncontested, even gallop that suits the horses tracking him.
scenarios.body: Trio controls the tempo from the front, with Hengest and Perfect Scoundrel sitting close enough to pounce turning for home; the measured pace on Good To Soft means no one is softened up unduly and those who travel prominently conserve energy for a sustained Epsom finish. This is the most likely shape given the lone front-runner dynamic and suits horses with a clean prominent racing style that can quicken off a steady pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Trio Fades, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Trio's inexperience over 1m2f on soft ground causes him to tie up in the final two furlongs, opening the race to horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Trio's form is largely over shorter trips and any sign of him emptying after setting his own pace would create a vacuum that mid-to-rear horses could exploit; Almekarem, with Prescott's patient placement and a recent win, and Crystal Pier would be best positioned to benefit. However, many of the genuine hold-up runners here have been redistributed to midfield positions that are not their natural station, tempering the probability of a clean closing scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Staying Test
scenarios.trigger: If Trio slows the race to a crawl and the final quarter-mile becomes a gruelling stamina examination on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: A dawdle followed by a punishing finish on soft turf at Epsom would expose any horse lacking genuine stamina; Arthur's Realm, with his best form in soft conditions over 12f, and Almekarem would be better suited than shorter-speed types. Perfect Scoundrel, who has won at the trip, could also feature though much depends on whether the finish becomes an extreme stamina test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hidden Speed Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up type manages to find a prominent position early and benefits from racing against their typical pattern.
scenarios.body: Mao Shang Wong or Sail On Sailor, if able to secure an unexpectedly forward position in a small 10-runner field, could race with more momentum than usual and catch the field off guard; however, both carry STYLE_FIT discounts precisely because racing out of role is a genuine cost not a free upgrade. The probability is low because the structural pace map does not invite this outcome, and their soft-ground records are limited.

watchPoints.text: Watch Trio's stride and head carriage from the two-furlong pole — if he shows signs of tying up on the soft ground having never raced beyond 8f, the race opens dramatically for Perfect Scoundrel and Almekarem who are best placed to pounce.

Hengest's soft-going record is a single run with no win or place; Jason Watson will need to nurse him through any sticky patches at Epsom, and if the ground rides testing, his chance could diminish quickly despite the prominent position.

Monitor the early positions of Mao Shang Wong, Hello Cotai and Sail On Sailor — if any of them push forward against their natural tendency to secure a better berth, it could inject unexpected pace pressure on Trio and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Arthur's Realm has run 12 times on soft ground and remains competitive in this going, but five consecutive runs without a finish better than fifth suggest his ability to win off OR=76 may have stalled — watch for whether his soft-ground stamina becomes a factor if the race truly tests.

Almekarem's trainer Sir Mark Prescott rarely runs horses without a clear plan; a 19-day turnaround after a seventh on 12f Good suggests a deliberate step back in distance today, and if the hold-up shape materialises, he is the horse most likely to benefit from Prescott's angle.

races.name: Geoff Lewis Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: H Key Lails
runners_data.comment: H Key Lails has winning form in his recent starts, scoring four starts back, and has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; the main risk is that his last three outings have yielded three finishes outside the places, suggesting he must recapture earlier form.

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Tom Queally partners this six-year-old who wants to come from well off the pace, but with multiple hold-up types in the field he is squeezed into a more active role that doesn't suit — his two placings in fifteen similar-going runs underline that soft ground is already a stretch, and racing against his grain compounds that.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner three starts back, Oj Lifestyle brings solid recent form into this and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; rated 78 and the top-ranked runner in the field, he looks the one to beat off 139 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Amused
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle has kept this four-year-old busy (run six days ago) and Luke Catton's 3lb claim helps at the weights, but Amused is at heart a hold-up horse who has finished placed in soft-ground handicaps at this distance before; the redistribution to midfield means he travels closer than ideal, softening what was already a modest strike rate on testing ground.
runners_data.comment: Amused has been placed twice in his last three starts, including a runner-up finish two starts back and again three starts back, and he has run over today's distance and going before; winless in recent starts is the concern, and that seventh last time out gives some pause.

runners_data.name: Here I Bow
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Oli Rix's small yard with a form string full of mid-pack finishes and zero wins; good to soft at Epsom over this longer trip looks like a significant ask, and the horse has produced nothing in similar conditions across eight runs to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Here I Bow has run over today's trip before but arrives winless in her last five starts, her best recent effort a second five starts back, and a fifth last time out eleven days ago does little to inspire confidence, though the quick return suggests she is at least fit.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old is the most credible prominent racer in the field, with two wins from ten furlongs on good ground and a reliable record of finishing placed; Jason Watson is an experienced handler of this type, and stepping back slightly in trip to the mile-and-a-half at Epsom could actually expose rivals' stamina rather than his own.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into seventh last time out, Super Hit faces an uphill task on our figures, ranked seventh of eight, though he has run over today's trip and shown ability in recent starts, including two wins in his last six; a trainer striking at just 5% is an added concern.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for Simon Dow; Tyler Heard can dictate entirely on his own terms, and two wins from fifteen runs in similar conditions shows the horse can handle the ground — the key risk is whether the extra half-furlong beyond his most recent winning trip on soft exposes a stamina ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Tronido has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround, but her recent form reads patchy — a winner five starts back, she has since posted a fourth, an unplaced effort, a seventh and a fifth, leaving plenty to prove under 132 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Eduardo Calderon
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's three-year-old has run consistently in the placed positions at seven furlongs on soft and good-to-soft, and Kaiya Fraser partners a horse who will push forward into second or third early; the step up to mile-and-a-half is an unknown for a horse whose entire form profile is over shorter trips, but the prominent position suits the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but Eduardo Calderon has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out and a second four starts back, and he arrives here fit on 12 days' rest, suited by today's going, and with our rating of 78 suggesting he holds more in hand than his official mark implies; the risk is he has yet to convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Uniter
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's three-year-old carries the lowest OR in the field at 58 and a form string featuring a pulled-up run and two figures-of-no-merit finishes; Saffie Osborne partners, but a horse whose best soft-ground effort is a single placing over six furlongs is deeply exposed here, and being pushed out of a natural rearward position into midfield adds further complication.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pull-up among those efforts and no finish better than fifth, Uniter is hard to fancy at the foot of the ratings here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 12-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Tronido is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the gates at his own tempo around Epsom's unique undulating mile-and-a-half layout. Super Hit and Eduardo Calderon will push forward to track closely in second and third, creating a small, contained group up front while the rest settle behind. On Good To Soft ground at Epsom, a lone leader setting a sustainable gallop is rarely run down late, especially over this trip where stamina is tested through the long home straight — this race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses with proven soft-ground stamina who can close steadily rather than sprint. The field nominally contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Oj Lifestyle, Amused, and Uniter are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning they are unlikely to secure their preferred rearward position and the prominent/tracking profile is the one best placed to exploit this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tronido Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tronido bowls along at a comfortable solo gallop and the prominent pair never apply enough pressure to force a true test.
scenarios.body: Tronido dictates every yard on Good To Soft ground, conserving enough energy to hold on through the Epsom straight while rivals burn stamina chasing; Super Hit and Eduardo Calderon, tracking closely, are best placed of the chasers to reel him in if he ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit or Eduardo Calderon press Tronido early enough to expose his stamina limitations on this testing ground.
scenarios.body: The pace lifts fractionally through the home turn as the prominent pair close ranks, and Tronido's form over seven furlongs on soft looks more natural than this extra distance; Super Hit's repeated placed efforts over ten furlongs on Good ground suggest the step back in trip here actually suits his one-paced staying style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to set up a strong late run from the real hold-up types despite their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: Key Lails is the one genuine hold-up horse not redistributed and carries good soft-ground form, able to launch from off the pace if the leaders have burnt each other; Oj Lifestyle and Amused, both mapped out of their natural role, would need a truly strong gallop to find clear running late and the style-fit discount materially reduces their chance here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates, the pace is erratic, and multiple horses race wide or get shuffled back at Epsom's tricky bends.
scenarios.body: Here I Bow's raw inexperience at three and Uniter's modest form string make them each live outsiders if the race falls apart in scrappy fashion; neither has the profile to be relied upon, but both carry low weights and could outrun their odds in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tronido's jumping-off point at the start — if Tyler Heard is slow away or another horse dashes up to challenge him to the first bend, the unchallenged-leader scenario collapses and the entire pace map shifts.

Super Hit has headgear (hood/tongue tie) and an active trainer record (2/41 over 14 days); if Jason Watson sends him forward more aggressively than expected, he could crowd Tronido's space and force a falsely run early pace that would benefit closers.

Oj Lifestyle, Amused, and Uniter are all genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield by the race shape — if they bunch in behind the prominent group through Epsom's twisting early bends, traffic trouble in the straight becomes a real risk that could produce chaotic late results.

The going is officially Good to Soft at 4:40, but the repeated identical going reports across all races suggest the clerk's description has not updated dynamically — monitor any racecourse updates as soft or wetter ground would hit the prominent runners harder and lengthen the race for the true hold-up types.

Eduardo Calderon is unproven beyond seven furlongs and steps up significantly in trip here; watch in-running to see whether Kaiya Fraser is able to hold a prominent position through the first half of the race or whether the horse weakens once the stamina test begins in earnest.

races.name: Betfred 'play Fred's £5 Million' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: French Affair
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground over 6f but has mixed form at 7f; Jennie Candlish's yard is 3/15 over 14 days showing active form, and this 3yo steps back to soft for the first time in recent starts — the going is likely fine but the 7f trip on Epsom's undulating track has previously returned a 6th; a prominent position just off Million Gold looks natural and exploitable.
runners_data.comment: French Affair arrives here in the form of his life, back-to-back wins making him the one to beat, and he has experience of both today's trip and going. Carrying 138 lb from stall three after 23 days off, his rating of 90 underlines his clear class advantage.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride for George Margarson, whose yard is flat (0/5 T14); a confirmed hold-up horse whose single recent placing in 15 similar-going runs is a concern, and the 8-day turnaround after finishing 3rd over 7f on Good may mean the yard is happy with fitness levels — needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Dapper Guest has run over today's trip and going, and his third last time out suggests a return to form is brewing, with just eight days between runs keeping him sharp; yet to score in recent starts is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton sends this 5yo out 25 days fresh on Good to Soft with a headgear flag (p), and the horse has a placed effort at this trip in similar conditions; as a prominent runner with the ability to race just off the pace, the Epsom straight suits a horse that can be delivered without checking, and T14 of 3/27 suggests the stable is ticking over.
runners_data.comment: Silver Trumpet won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while his rating of 80 suggests he holds strong claims; the main risk is that fifth last time out leaves him needing to bounce back to his best.

runners_data.name: Million Gold
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3yo is the race's only true front-runner, returning after 65 days off; won over 6f on Soft/Standard at Southwell on a previous start and steps up to 7f, which is a question, but an uncontested lead on soft ground could compensate for the distance query — OR 75 is workable but the layoff and trip-up are the key risks to the controlling scenario.
runners_data.comment: Million Gold won three starts back but has been unplaced on his most recent outing, rates below his official mark on our figures, and 65 days off the track adds an extra question mark; he has run over today's trip and stall two are the slim upsides here.

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: Kieren Fox rides this lightly-weighted 3yo (128lbs, OR 72) who has shown glimpses at 7f on Good; 33 days between runs is not alarming but the yard (Attwater, 1/17 T14) is not in rampant form, and the hold-up style means Fresh Fade needs the pace to lift in the second half of this 7f — a real beneficiary only in Scenario B if the gallop sharpens.
runners_data.comment: Fresh Fade is winless in his last five starts, yet an 8 lb upgrade on his official mark suggests he is better than his recent figures imply, and he arrives here fresh after 33 days with experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that he must convert that latent ability into a finish.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's 4yo has strong raw form — two wins at 7-8f on Good — but is a genuine hold-up horse that the race map has redistributed to midfield because the rearward slots are over-populated; with a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 it is likely to race further back than shown and will need more pace than Million Gold alone can generate, making the positional disadvantage a meaningful discount on its prospects.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and the speed rating does little to inspire confidence, Play Me faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals, though he did win last time out and has run over today's trip, and 17 days represents a fair enough freshness angle.

races.paceDynamic: Million Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners and no other genuine leaders in the field, will stride to the front unchallenged and control a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Soft ground at Epsom. French Affair and Silver Trumpet will push forward to dispute prominent positions just behind the leader, creating a modest but organised pace that is unlikely to become truly searching. Dapper Guest, Fresh Fade, and Play Me — the hold-up brigade — will be forced to settle further back, though Play Me is a true hold-up type mapped to midfield simply because the rearward positions are over-subscribed; its actual racing position may be closer to the rear than the map suggests. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with strong finishing kicks, as the uncontested pace set by Million Gold on soft ground should compress the early splits and bring closers into play late, but the modest gallop equally allows the prominent horses French Affair and Silver Trumpet to coast into a winning position without burning too much fuel — making midfield-to-prominent types the primary beneficiaries if the pace stays conservative.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Million Gold Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Million Gold dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent horses coast up to challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Million Gold sets an economical pace that allows French Affair and Silver Trumpet to travel comfortably on his quarters before producing their finishing efforts from the two-furlong pole; on soft ground at Epsom the prominent stalker who gets a clear run widest into the straight will have the finishing position advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Come Late In Soft
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently mid-race to string out the field and set up a genuine late run.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace, aided by French Affair and Silver Trumpet pressing forward, creates enough early tempo for the hold-up horses to benefit from a true test of stamina on soft ground; Dapper Guest, who has placed at this trip on Good ground, is the likeliest beneficiary if able to find a clear passage around Epsom's turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop remains so controlled that Million Gold is never seriously pressed and simply stays on for a wire-to-wire win.
scenarios.body: On soft going a horse allowed to dictate its own fractions without a single rival willing to test it early can conserve enough energy to repel challengers in the final furlong; Million Gold's sole course of strength is front-running and at 3yo dropping into a weak handicap off a 65-day break, an untroubled lead could be decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If tactical confusion or shuffling in the straight creates a gap for a well-handicapped outsider to exploit.
scenarios.body: Play Me, though a genuine hold-up horse racing out of its natural position and tagged accordingly, has winning form at 7f on Good ground and could benefit from a chaotic finish if the front group ties up; its STYLE_FIT discount is real, but the raw form and OR of 66 gives marginal value in a small field if the race dissolves into a sprint.

watchPoints.text: Million Gold sets off unchallenged — watch whether Robert Havlin elects to bowl along or sit in a false rhythm, as the gallop he chooses in the first two furlongs will determine whether front or held-up horses are favoured.

French Affair drops from 6f wins to a 7f test on Epsom's unique camber — watch for any sign of greenness or drifting right-handed in the straight, which could cost a prominent horse vital lengths at the death.

Play Me is a true hold-up horse likely to find itself trapped in midfield rather than its natural rear position — watch for Donagh Murphy (claiming 7lbs) having to make an earlier-than-ideal move to avoid being boxed in on the turn.

Dapper Guest's headgear flag (p) and 8-day turnaround are worth monitoring in the paddock — if the horse looks fresh and well, the rapid reappearance could indicate the yard spotted a well-handicapped opportunity on soft ground.

Silver Trumpet's headgear (p) is also flagged — watch to see if it travels smoothly behind Million Gold in the early stages, as a horse that settles well in the prominent position is the most natural threat to the leader's supremacy from two furlongs out.
